What makes the dandelion so amazing?

Turning from a yellow flower into a white fluffy ball that flies off in the wind, the dandelion is one of children's favorite spring plants. There's science hidden in the seeds that scatter when you blow on them.

Curious about the story of the dandelion picture book? We look at the lessons of the dandelion picture book alongside the illustrations. Come meet the key scenes of the dandelion picture book's story too. Read the dandelion picture book together with your child and talk about the story.

content.alt: Dandelion - Nature and science facts about the dandelion
content.text:
Nature and science facts about the dandelion

A single dandelion flower is actually hundreds of tiny flowers gathered together. Each seed has a feathery parachute (pappus) that rides the wind far away, creating a column of air between the seeds so it can fly in a very stable way — an intricate structure. Its roots also dig deep into the ground, giving it the toughness to sprout again even when trampled or cut off at the top.

Points to observe together

Point out things like the flower (hundreds of tiny flowers), the seeds (parachutes), the roots (toughness), and how it spreads on the wind. It's fun to talk together about "How do the seeds fly away when you blow on them?"

Parent guide — extending through observation and hands-on play

On a spring or fall walk, blow on a dandelion seed head and send the seeds flying yourself. Observe the seed's parachute with a magnifying glass, and it's fun to draw the life cycle as it changes from yellow flower → fluffy ball → seeds.

content.text:
Frequently Asked Questions (FAQ)

Q. Is a dandelion a single flower?
A. No. It looks like one flower, but it's actually hundreds of tiny flowers gathered together.

Q. How do dandelion seeds fly so far?
A. Each has a feathery parachute (pappus) that rides the wind, creating a column of air so it flies far in a stable way.

Q. How can we observe them at home?
A. Blowing the fluff, observing the parachute with a magnifying glass, and drawing the yellow flower → fluffy ball life cycle are all fun.
